said: I'll start by getting the project's current state.
Working on bodea. Let me check the project state and endpoints.
Now let me test the catalog directly and look at the page.
Catalog is fine — 30 products return under the Bodea scope. Now the storefront config and the page.
Local config is correct. Checking what the live site actually serves and what pages exist.
Config is correct and live. Now the pages — the homepage links to `/racks`, `/switching`, etc.
The PLP points at category path `products/racks`. Let me verify that category exists.
`products/racks` doesn't exist. Let me find the real category paths.
Two things surfacing. Let me confirm.
`products/racks` does exist (my earlier lookup used the wrong argument type) and returns 9 products. So catalog and page config both look right. Let me check the block and load the page for real.
Block exists. Let me load the live page and watch what it actually does.
Real signal now. Two candidates: the block crashed, and the query has a visibility filter. Let me test both.
The data is there — the page's own query returns 9 products. The block itself is crashing. Line 137 is `provider.render(SortBy, {})($productSort)`.
Local source is unmodified and looks correct. But the error is on the live site — let me compare what's actually deployed.
That was just gzip. Let me decompress and diff properly.
Deployed code is byte-identical to the template. Let me inspect the actual DOM state in the browser.
Key detail: `.search__product-sort` exists but is empty, and the product list is empty. Facets rendered. So SortBy specifically failed. Let me check its import.
Let me reproduce the exact failing call to get the full error.
My test harness called it wrong — `provider.render(...)` is the method. Redoing:
SortBy renders fine when I invoke it manually now — so the element and container are both healthy. This looks like a load-time race. Let me check reproducibility.
Confirmed the throw is `if(!t) throw new Error("Root element is not defined")` — the target element was null at that moment. Let me test whether it's a race by re-running decorate now.
Deterministic, not a race. Let me look at the exact deployed lines around the failure.
Found it — the selectors themselves are failing. Only `.search__facets` matches; every class with a hyphen fails. Let me see what actually survived parsing.
`Element.querySelector` finds it but `DocumentFragment.querySelector` doesn't. Let me isolate that precisely.
This result shouldn't be possible per spec — let me verify it isn't an artifact of my test harness by running the same check on a blank page.
This fails even on a blank page, which is not real browser behavior — my harness is suspect. Let me test it decisively.
Hyphens work fine in isolation, so that theory was wrong. Let me dump the actual parsed structure.

My in-page test harness is returning self-contradictory results (it lists the elements via `querySelectorAll` but fails to find them via `querySelector` in the same call), so I'm discarding that line of testing. Let me verify the remaining leads with reliable tools.
The screenshot confirms it: the page renders only the heading, no products at all. And `head.html` line 100 is missing the CSP nonce every other script has. Let me read the custom code in head.html.
Let me check whether this is PLP-only or affects products site-wide.
The homepage shows a real live product (VR Rack, $7,500 — pulled from the catalog). So the commerce plumbing works end to end. Let me confirm the failure is all category pages, not just `/racks`.
Same crash on `/switching`. Let me check one plausible cause — a version mismatch between the block and the deployed dropin libraries.
That's a strong lead. Let me check it across the dropins.

It's the page — specifically the category-listing block. The catalog and the storefront configuration are both fine.

## What I checked

**Catalog — healthy.** 30 products, correctly scoped to Bodea. I ran the exact query the category page fires (category `products/racks`, plus its visibility filter) and it returned all 9 rack products.

**Storefront configuration — correct.** The live site's config has the right store, website, and store-view codes and the right Commerce endpoint. The proof it works end to end: your homepage shows a real live product pulled from the catalog — VR Rack, $7,500, with working Details and Add to Cart buttons.

**The page — broken.** The block that draws the product grid crashes while loading, before it draws anything. It happens on every category page (I confirmed `/racks` and `/switching`). The page itself is authored correctly — it points at a real category that has products. The heading renders, then nothing.

## What I could not pin down

I don't know why that block crashes. The deployed block code is byte-for-byte identical to the stock storefront template, and the element it complains is missing is right there in that template. So it isn't something you customized.

My leading suspect, unconfirmed: the shared UI library on the site is version 2.0.1, but the product-discovery library that powers the category grid asks for 1.9.x. The crash is thrown from inside that shared library. Against this theory — the product detail library has the same mismatch and works fine. So treat it as a lead, not a conclusion.

## Two real defects I did confirm

- Every label file (`/placeholders/*.json`) returns 404. The block loads these first thing.
- `head.html` loads `bodea-customer-group.js` without the security token every other script tag has, so the browser blocks it on every page.

Both are worth fixing regardless.

## Suggested next step

Reinstall the storefront dependencies and republish, so the shared library and the product-discovery library are on matching versions. That's the cheapest test of the leading theory. Want me to do that?

One aside: the "Catalog Highlights" section on your homepage is hardcoded text, not real catalog data, and its six product images are broken. That's a separate content problem from the category pages.
